main: The split of big-four hyperscaler 2027 AI accelerator spending between custom ASIC racks and Nvidia GPU racks

extras.text: the split of the 19.5 GW of incremental compute capacity projected for 2027 (the same ASIC-vs-GPU mix counted in gigawatts)
a growing share (compared with the hyperscalers' current ASIC share)
cost-per-gigawatt estimate of $6-11 billion for Broadcom/Marvell ASIC racks
roughly $19 billion per gigawatt for Nvidia GB300-based racks
$25 billion per gigawatt under Vera Rubin

why: The thesis tracks one 2027 ASIC-vs-GPU spending mix; the gigawatt split is the same mix in another unit, and the cost-per-gigawatt figures are the article's reason for the shift, not a yardstick a spending split can be measured against.

main: The combined new HBM capacity the three producers add in 2027

extras.text: whether any of it arrives before late 2027
easing the shortage and the record HBM prices that gate NVIDIA's GPU output
the item's forecast that no new HBM supply arrives before late 2027

why: The full-year amount of new capacity and whether any of it lands before late 2027 can move apart (a large amount arriving only in the fourth quarter), and the article's matter is the timing of supply relief, which an analyst would hold apart from the size of the year's additions.

main: Combined calendar-2026 data-center capital expenditure of the big four AI hyperscalers

extras.text: the ~$650 billion plan reported in the item
NVIDIA's ~$1 trillion projection for 2027

why: One 2026 spending total is tracked; the $650 billion plan and the $1 trillion figure are yardsticks only, though the $1 trillion belongs to 2027 and is a mismatched yardstick for a 2026 total rather than a second tracked quantity.

main: Whether Nvidia closes the announced $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face by about 2028-03-05

extras.text: abandons/restructures the purchase
an acquisition that would absorb cash and add a developer-platform asset

why: One deal-closing event is tracked; abandonment or restructuring is the same deal's other outcome and the cash and asset effects are consequences, not tracked.

main: The amount of credit support / backstop commitments NVIDIA reports backing AI cloud partners' compute procurement, at its FY2027 annual report

extras.text: the resulting credit-risk exposure
whether it materially raises NVIDIA's contingent obligations
the revenue-sharing side of the new model, named in the question

why: One reported amount of credit support is tracked; the credit-risk exposure and contingent-obligation effect are the consequence of that same amount, and the revenue share is only the name of the model.

main: The combined calendar-2026 revenue of the four hyperscalers' in-house AI accelerator programmes (Trainium, TPU, Maia, MTIA)

extras.text: or disclosed shipment volume
competing with NVIDIA GPUs, whose customers also fund NVIDIA's data center segment

why: One combined 2026 custom-silicon quantity is tracked, which the article treats as one matter; shipment volume is a fallback measure of the same programmes, not a second card, and the competitive link to NVIDIA is background.

main: Confirmation that first Vera Rubin shipments have begun by end of calendar 2026

extras.text: slipping into 2027 or later
the product line that carries its data center value

why: One shipping-start event is tracked; a slip into 2027 is that event's other outcome and the product's importance is background.

main: The French competition authority's decision concluding its antitrust investigation into NVIDIA, by late January 2027

extras.text: any fine or behavioral remedies imposed
closure, as one form the conclusion can take

why: One regulatory decision event is tracked; the fine, remedies or closure are the content of that same decision, which the article treats as one matter nearing a conclusion.
